 Menu Home › GROCER GROCER Target's First-Ever Black Friday Food & Beverage Drops Signal a New Retail Playbook
 Nov 17, 2026 Advertisement For years, the "drop" has belonged to sneakers, streetwear and limited-edition toys. This Black Friday, Target is moving that same scarcity-and-hype playbook into the grocery aisle—and the food and beverage industry should be paying attention.
 On Tuesday, Target announced its Black Friday plans, and tucked inside the usual flood of gift deals is something new: the retailer's first-ever Black Friday food and beverage exclusive drops . Launching Friday, Nov. 27, the lineup pairs buzzy better-for-you and fan-favorite brands with blind boxes, collectibles and giveaways—treating snacks and cereal like coveted limited releases rather than commodity SKUs.
 Inside Target's First-Ever Black Friday Food & Beverage Drops
 Three brands anchor the debut, each leaning into exclusivity, collectibility and creator-driven hype:
 Advertisement 
 GOODLES: Buy one, get one free on Twirly Mac in-store and online, plus an exclusive, limited-time mac & cheese plushie for $10, available in store only.
 Katjes x Jake Shane: An exclusive Mystery Sourpuss blind box featuring a pack of Sourpuss gummy candy and a collectible phone mount for $9.99—a $20 value.
 Backflip Cereal: A buy one, get one 50% off offer, plus a new seasonal cereal drop featuring hidden collectible cards from co-founder Ben Azelart.
 That Backflip drop is where the gamification gets serious. Select hidden cards unlock prizes, including:
 An all-expenses-paid trip to Southern California to meet Ben and tour his YouTube studio (10 winners)
 A $1,000 Target GiftCard (10 winners)
 A one-year supply of Backflip (100 winners)
 The common thread? Every drop comes wrapped in a reason to act fast, share online, and come back. Blind boxes, plushies, hidden cards and creator meetups are the toolkit of collectible culture—now applied to center-store CPG.
 A Weeklong Wave of Holiday Food and Beverage Deals
 Beyond the headline drops, Target is running weeklong food and beverage savings from Nov. 22-29 , aimed at holiday hosts, gift-givers and stocking-stuffer shoppers:
 Target favorites: Buy one, get one 50% off on select products including Backflip Cereal, Favorite Day, and Good & Gather snacks and candy.
 Holiday gifting and sweets: Buy one, get one 50% off food and beverage Advent calendars and select packaged chocolate and non-chocolate candy, plus 15% off Marks & Spencer candy gifts and 15% off Hickory Farms gifts.
 Wine and beer: Buy four bottles of wine and save 20%.
 It's a full-funnel seasonal push: splashy limited drops to drive foot traffic and social buzz, backed by broad everyday savings to convert the browse into a basket.
 Advertisement 
 Why It Matters
 For grocers, CPG brands and foodservice buyers, Target's move is a signal worth reading closely. The "product drop" model—long native to fashion and collectibles—has officially crossed into food and beverage retail at national scale. That reframes how emerging and challenger brands can earn shelf velocity.
 A few practical takeaways for operators and brand teams:
 Scarcity sells center store. Pairing a BOGO with a limited plushie, blind box or collectible card turns a routine purchase into an event—and gives shoppers a reason to post, which is free reach.
 Creator equity is distribution equity. Backflip's Ben Azelart and Katjes' Jake Shane tie-ins show that founder and influencer audiences can be activated right at the shelf. For buyers evaluating new brands, built-in creator reach is now a real merchandising asset.
 Better-for-you brands fit the hype format. GOODLES and Backflip both play in the elevated, functional-leaning snack space—proof that "better-for-you" and "buzzworthy" are no longer mutually exclusive on the planogram.
 Bundle the gift occasion. Advent calendars, curated candy gifts and multi-bottle wine deals show how to capture holiday hosting and gifting dollars—an approach independent grocers and specialty retailers can mirror at their own scale.
 For procurement directors and category managers, the lesson is clear: the brands winning placement this season aren't just competing on price—they're competing on cultural relevance and collectibility.
 The Bigger F&B Trend
 Target's drop strategy lands amid a broader wave of brand collaborations and hype-driven launches reshaping the food and beverage industry—from co-branded LTOs to collectible-fueled cereal plays. We've seen the same energy in launches like Disney+ and Tiff's Treats' blue chocolate chip cookies and CELSIUS's Costco-exclusive holiday "Cheers Pack." The common denominator: retailers and brands are chasing engagement, not just transactions.

 Shoppers can see Target's weekly ad for full details on the Nov. 22-29 deals and the Nov. 27 drops.
